source_text: Ἔγνων δὲ ταῦτα ἐγὼ ἅπαντα, σοφίαν ἐκ Θεοῦ λαβὼν, ἣν ὕστερον ἀποβαλὼν, οὐκέτι οἷός τε ἤμην ὅμοιος εἶναι. Ἔφυγε γὰρ ἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ σοφία εἰς μῆκος ἄπειρον, καὶ εἰς βάθος ἀμέτρητον, ὡς μὴ εἶναι αὐτῆς λαβέσθαι μηκέτι. Ὥστε ὕστερον καὶ τοῦ ἐπιζητεῖν αὐτὴν, τέλειον ἀπεσχόμην· καὶ οὔτε ἐνεθυμούμην ἔτι τοῦ κατανοεῖν τὰς τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀφροσύνας καὶ βουλὰς ματαίας, καὶ ἀλύοντα βίον. Οὕτω δὲ διακείμενος, εἰς αὐτὰ διηνέχθην, καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ συσχεθεὶς θανατηφόρῳ, ἔγνων τὴν γυναῖκα, γῆν τινα, ἢ εἴ τι ἕτερον τοιοῦτον ὑπάρχουσαν. Καρδία μὲν γὰρ αὐτῆς σαγηνεύει τοὺς παριόντας, χειρὶ δὲ χεῖρα συνάψασα μόνον, κατέχει ἢ εἰ δεσμοῖς περιβάλλουσα εἷλκε. Μόνος δ᾽ ἂν ἀπ᾽ αὐτῆς ῥυσθείης, τὸν Θεὸν ἵλεω καὶ ἐπόπτην ἐσχηκώς· ὡς ὅ γε ἁμαρτίᾳ δεδουλωμένος οὐκ ἂν ἐκφύγοι. Ζητήσας δ᾽ ἐγὼ διὰ πασῶν γυναικῶν σωφροσύνην αὐτῶν, εὗρον ἐν οὐδεμιᾷ. Καὶ ἄνδρα μέν τις ἐν χιλίοις γνοίη ἂν σώφρονα, γυναῖκα δὲ οὔ. Κατενόησα δὲ ἐκεῖνο μάλιστα, ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ὑπὸ Θεοῦ ἁπλοῖ ταῖς ψυχαῖς γενόμενοι, ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισπῶνται λογισμοὺς ποικίλους καὶ ζητήσεις ἀπεράντους, καὶ σοφίαν ζητεῖν προσποιούμενοι, περὶ ῥημάτια κατατρίβονται.
thought_title: Solomon's loss of wisdom, entanglement with a deadly woman, and reflection on human perversity
orientation: Solomon, having received wisdom from God and then cast it away, describes how wisdom fled from him irretrievably, how he ceased seeking it and turned to a death-bringing desire for a woman who ensnares men, and how he found no soberness among women; he concludes by observing that humans, made simple by God, entangle themselves in endless devices and wear themselves out over trifles while pretending to seek wisdom.
pass_a_gloss: I came to know all these things, I, having taken wisdom from God; which later having cast away, I was no longer able to be like. For wisdom fled from me into infinite length, and into immeasurable depth, so that there was no longer any taking hold of it. So that afterwards also I ceased completely from seeking it; and neither was I considering any longer to understand the folly and empty counsels of the ungodly, and a wandering life. Thus disposed, I was carried into them, and bound fast by a death-bearing desire, I knew the woman, some earth, or if anything else of such a kind existing. For her heart hunts the passers-by, but by merely joining hand to hand she holds as firmly as if she had wrapped him in bonds and dragged him off. One alone would be rescued from her, having God as propitious and overseer; for the one enslaved to sin would not escape. And I, having sought sobriety through all women, found it in not one. And a man one among a thousand one would know as sober, but a woman not. And I perceived that especially, that humans having become simple in souls by God, draw upon themselves varied reasonings and endless searches, and pretending to seek wisdom, they wear themselves out over little words.

lemmas.gloss: I came to know / I knew (aorist active indicative 1st sg.)
having taken / having received (aorist active participle nominative masculine singular)
having cast away / having thrown off (aorist active participle nominative masculine singular)
completely / utterly (adverb, accusative neuter singular used adverbially)
I ceased / I abstained (aorist middle indicative 1st sg.)
being disposed / situated thus (present middle/passive participle nominative masculine singular)
bound fast / held fast / entangled (aorist passive participle nominative masculine singular)
death-bearing / death-bringing (dative feminine singular adjective agreeing with ἐπιθυμίᾳ)
hunts with a dragnet / ensnares / hunts (present active indicative 3rd sg.)
having been enslaved / enslaved (perfect passive participle nominative masculine singular)
they wear themselves out / they waste away (present middle/passive indicative 3rd pl.)

choices.why: Active reception of a gift; 'taken' preserves the aorist participle's sense of a discrete act of receiving.
Τέλειον functions adverbially to intensify the cessation; 'completely' captures the force without adding a noun.

choices.term: γῆν τινα, ἢ εἴ τι ἕτερον τοιοῦτον ὑπάρχουσαν
choices.english: some earth, or if anything else of such a kind existing
choices.why: The text portrays the woman as 'earth' (dust/clay) and leaves open any similar thing; 'existing' renders ὑπάρχουσαν as a participle.
rejected: a certain earth, or whatever other such thing there might be
some land, or if any other such thing subsisting

choices.why: Σαγηνεύω derives from σαγήνη (dragnet); the verb means to catch by dragging a net, hence 'ensnares' but with the net image.
ἁπλοῖ (dative plural of ἁπλοῦς) means simple, unmixed, not compound; 'simple in souls' keeps the dative of respect.

choices.english: they wear themselves out over little words
choices.why: ῥημάτια are diminutive 'little words/trifles'; κατατρίβω in middle/passive means to wear oneself out by rubbing/grinding.
rejected: they waste away over trivial sayings
they grind themselves down over words
they exhaust themselves about small matters

bible_refs.note: Ἐγὼ πάντα ἐδοκίμασα ἐν σοφίᾳ — parallel of testing all things in wisdom
καὶ εὑρίσκω πικρυτέραν ἀπὸ θανάτου τὴν γυναῖκα — woman more bitter than death
ἄνδρα μέν τις ἐν χιλίοις εὗρον, γυναῖκα δὲ ἐν πᾶσιν ταύταις οὐχ εὗρον — one man among a thousand, no woman
ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησεν τὸν ἄνθρωπον εὐθύ, αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐζήτησαν λογισμούς πολλούς — God made man upright, they sought many devices
ἐκκλῖναι ἀπὸ γυναικὸς πονηρᾶς — to turn away from an evil woman; heart as snare
γλυκύτερα μέλι στόμει γυναικός — woman's lips drip honey; feet go down to death

pass_b_english: I came to know all these things, having taken wisdom from God. Later I cast it away, and I was no longer capable of being like what I had been. For wisdom fled from me into an infinite length and into an immeasurable depth, so that it was no longer possible to grasp it. Consequently I completely ceased even from seeking it afterward. Nor did I any longer set my mind on understanding the follies and empty counsels of the godless, and a life that wanders. In such a disposition I was carried into those things, and being bound fast by a death-bearing desire, I knew the woman—some earth, or if anything else of such a kind existing. For her heart hunts with a dragnet those who pass by; but by merely joining hand to hand she holds a man as firmly as if she had wrapped him in bonds and dragged him off. One alone would be rescued from her, having God as propitious and overseeing; for the one who has been enslaved by sin would not escape. Seeking through all women their self-control, I found it in not one. And one might find a self-controlled man among a thousand, but not a woman. I considered this especially: that human beings, having become simple in souls by God, draw upon themselves varied reasonings and endless inquiries, and pretending to seek wisdom, they wear themselves out over little words.

problems.quote: she only holds, or if she surrounds with bonds she drags away
problems.source_quote: κατέχει ἢ εἰ δεσμοῖς περιβάλλουσα εἷλκε
problems.why: ἢ εἰ is a comparison: by a mere joining of hands she holds him as firmly as if she had bound and dragged him. The English makes it an alternative.
problems.fix: by merely joining hand to hand she holds a man as firmly as if she had wrapped him in bonds and dragged him off.
problems.ruling: μόνον … κατέχει ἢ εἰ … εἷλκε compares a mere handclasp to binding and dragging; ἢ εἰ means “as if,” not the alternative “or if.”

edits.old: For her heart hunts with a dragnet those who pass by; but joining hand to hand, she only holds, or if she surrounds with bonds she drags away.
edits.new: For her heart hunts with a dragnet those who pass by; but by merely joining hand to hand she holds a man as firmly as if she had wrapped him in bonds and dragged him off.

fixed: The translation made ἢ εἰ (as if) into an alternative (or if). Fixed to a comparative: 'as firmly as if she had wrapped him in bonds and dragged him off.'

last_rejected.quote: I knew the woman—some earth, or if anything else of such a kind existing
last_rejected.source_quote: ἔγνων τὴν γυναῖκα, γῆν τινα, ἢ εἴ τι ἕτερον τοιοῦτον ὑπάρχουσαν
last_rejected.why: The apposition does not parse; ὑπάρχουσαν predicates what the woman is.
last_rejected.fix: I knew the woman as some earth, or as anything else of that kind.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπάρχουσαν agrees with τὴν γυναῖκα, so the sense 'the woman being some earth or the like' is kept. The English is clumsy but understandable, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: by merely joining hand to hand she holds a man as firmly as if she had wrapped him in bonds and dragged him off
last_rejected.source_quote: χειρὶ δὲ χεῖρα συνάψασα μόνον, κατέχει ἢ εἰ δεσμοῖς περιβάλλουσα εἷλκε
last_rejected.why: ἢ εἰ marks an alternative action, not a comparison of equal firmness.
last_rejected.fix: By merely joining hand to hand she holds him, or if she wraps him in bonds, she drags him.
last_rejected.ruling: κατέχει ἢ εἰ ... εἷλκε is a comparison ('holds as if/than if she had dragged him in bonds'). 'As firmly as if' fits the sense.
